_about: Batch B2 writer: terms for learn/batching, learn/gpus-kernels, learn/parallelism, learn/moe, learn/number-formats.

batch.short: The tokens of many sequences that the engine sends to the model together, in one step. The model reads its weights once for the whole batch.

static-batching.short: Batching where a fixed group of requests runs until the last one ends. New requests wait for the next group.

continuous-batching.short: Batching where the engine makes a new batch in every step. A finished sequence leaves at once, and a waiting request can join at the next step.

padding.short: Filler values that make all rows of a tensor the same length. The device computes them, but the results are not used.

packed-batch.short: A batch that puts the tokens of all sequences end to end in one dimension, with no padding. A cu_seqlens tensor marks where each sequence starts.

cu-seqlens.short: Cumulative sequence lengths: an int32 tensor of num_seqs + 1 values. Sequence i owns the packed tokens cu_seqlens[i] to cu_seqlens[i+1] - 1.

hbm.short: High Bandwidth Memory: the main memory of a GPU or NPU. It holds the weights and the KV cache. It is large but slow when compared with on-chip memory.

smem.short: SMEM. Fast on-chip memory inside each SM, up to about 228 KiB on recent NVIDIA GPUs. The threads of one thread block use it to share data.

register.short: The fastest storage on a GPU. Each thread has its own registers. An SM has a fixed register file (256 KiB on recent NVIDIA GPUs).

kernel-launch.short: The CPU tells the device to run one kernel with a grid of thread blocks. Each launch costs a few microseconds of CPU time.

cuda-stream.short: A queue of device work. Work in one stream runs in order. Work in different streams can overlap.

cuda-event.short: A marker that the CPU records in a stream. The CPU or another stream can wait until the device reaches the marker.

gemm.short: General matrix multiply: C = A × B. For A [M, K] and B [K, N] it does 2·M·N·K floating-point operations. Most model work is GEMMs.

tensor-core.short: A unit in an NVIDIA SM that multiplies small matrix tiles in one instruction. It gives most of the FLOP/s of the GPU, mainly in BF16, FP8 and FP4.

arithmetic-intensity.short: The floating-point operations of a kernel divided by the bytes it moves to and from memory (FLOP per byte).

roofline.short: A simple model of speed: a kernel runs at min(peak FLOP/s, bandwidth × arithmetic intensity). It tells if a kernel is memory-bound or compute-bound.

memory-bound.short: A kernel whose time is set by how fast it moves bytes, not by its math. Its arithmetic intensity is below the ridge point of the device.

compute-bound.short: A kernel whose time is set by its math (FLOPs), not by memory traffic. Its arithmetic intensity is above the ridge point of the device.

tensor-parallelism.short: TP. Each weight matrix is split across devices; each device computes a part of every layer, and an all-reduce adds the parts. DeepInfer does not use it.

pipeline-parallelism.short: PP. The layers are split into stages on different devices, and activations go from stage to stage. DeepInfer does not use it.

all-reduce.short: A collective: each rank gives a tensor, and each rank gets the element-wise sum (or max, min) of all of them.

all-gather.short: A collective: each rank gives one part, and each rank gets all parts joined in rank order.

all-to-all.short: A collective: each rank sends a different part of its data to each other rank. MoE dispatch and combine use this pattern.

broadcast.short: A collective: one rank (the source) sends the same tensor to all other ranks of the group.

nvlink.short: NVIDIA's fast link between GPUs in one machine or rack. It is much faster than the network between machines.

expert.short: One small feed-forward network inside an MoE layer. A token uses only the few experts that the router selects for it.

router.short: The small layer in an MoE layer that gives each token a score for each expert and selects the top-k experts. DeepInfer calls it the gate.

top-k-routing.short: Each token goes to the k experts with the highest router scores. Their outputs are added with weights that come from the scores.

shared-expert.short: An expert that every token uses, in addition to its top-k routed experts. It holds knowledge that all tokens need.

load-balance.short: How evenly the tokens spread over the experts (and over the devices that hold them). A busy expert makes all other devices wait.

expert-capacity.short: A fixed maximum number of tokens that one expert takes in one step. Some MoE systems drop the extra tokens. DeepInfer's code sets no capacity per expert.

ffn.short: Feed-forward network: the part of a transformer layer after attention. It works on each token alone, with two or three large matrix multiplies.

swiglu.short: A gated FFN form: out = W2 · (SiLU(W1·x) ⊙ (W3·x)). It needs three weight matrices instead of two.

active-parameters.short: The weights that one token really uses in a forward pass. In an MoE model this is much less than the total number of weights.

floating-point.short: A number stored as sign, exponent and mantissa bits: value = ±(1.mantissa) × 2^(exponent − bias). More exponent bits give more range; more mantissa bits give more precision.

mantissa.short: The fraction bits of a floating-point number. They set the precision: with m bits, the step between neighbour values is 2^−m times the power of two.

fp32.short: 32-bit floating point: 1 sign, 8 exponent and 23 mantissa bits. The reference format; 4 bytes per value.

bf16.short: bfloat16: 1 sign, 8 exponent and 7 mantissa bits. It has the range of FP32 with less precision; 2 bytes per value.

fp16.short: 16-bit floating point (half): 1 sign, 5 exponent and 10 mantissa bits. More precise than BF16, but the maximum is only 65,504.

e4m3.short: An FP8 format with 4 exponent and 3 mantissa bits. Its largest value is 448. DeepInfer uses it for FP8 weights and activations.

e5m2.short: An FP8 format with 5 exponent and 2 mantissa bits. It has more range (maximum 57,344) but less precision than E4M3. DeepInfer does not use it.

fp4.short: A 4-bit floating-point format. The usual layout is E2M1, which has only 16 codes: 0, ±0.5, ±1, ±1.5, ±2, ±3, ±4, ±6 (and −0).

ue8m0.short: An 8-bit unsigned scale format with exponent bits only: value = 2^(bits − 127). It can hold only powers of two.

block-scaling.short: A group of low-precision values (for example 16 or 32) shares one scale factor. The real value is code × scale. A small group keeps the error small.

mxfp4.short: Microscaling FP4 (OCP MX format): blocks of 32 E2M1 values that share one UE8M0 scale. That is 4.25 bits per value.

mxfp8.short: Microscaling FP8: blocks of 32 FP8 values (E4M3 in DeepInfer) that share one UE8M0 scale. That is 8.25 bits per value.

quantization.short: Storing numbers in a format with fewer bits, for example BF16 to FP8, with scale factors. It saves memory and bandwidth, and adds a small rounding error.
